tracks.title: Robovoice
tracks.summary: Cloud voice (Robovoice) is an optional, free alternative to local voice: connect your stack or Robovoice cloud, map agents to characters and see usage.
tracks.overview:
**Local voice** is InfiniBot's default and runs on your own computer. **Cloud voice (Robovoice)** is an optional, free choice you can pick instead. It plugs into InfiniBot's voice layer as a **voice provider**. When you pick it, voice sessions come from Robovoice and the mapped Robovoice character answers, using Robovoice's own speech-to-text → model → text-to-speech pipeline. Nothing switches to it unless you choose it, and you can go back to local voice any time.

This track covers the `/robovoice` page:
- **Voice provider.** Which provider serves voice (local by default), and what happens before you link.
- **Connection.** Self-hosted or Robovoice cloud, the URL, the edge device id and the write-only device key or edge token (from `robovoice login`).
- **Characters and pipelines.** Mapping each InfiniBot agent to a character and reading the effective STT → LLM → TTS chain, including self-host-only safety labels.
- **Fair use and tools.** How cloud voice stays free and fair, and the MCP endpoint Robovoice characters use to call InfiniBot tools.

The tours never save settings, link an account or start a call.

walkthroughs.title: Tour the Robovoice page
walkthroughs.summary: What each card on the Robovoice page does.

steps.title: Robovoice settings
steps.body: If you pick Cloud voice, your agents talk through Robovoice characters. This page is where you choose where Robovoice runs, map agents to characters and see usage.

steps.title: Which provider serves voice
steps.body: The top card shows which voice provider is active and whether it is ready. The same card appears in Setup › Voice.
steps.checkHint: Waiting for the Robovoice provider to register…

steps.title: Connection
steps.body: Where Robovoice runs, its URL and the credentials this gateway uses to reach it. Nothing here takes effect until you press **Save**.

steps.title: Usage
steps.body: Cloud voice is free. Usage is measured only to keep it fair for everyone, and if it's busy you can switch to local voice in one click.

steps.title: Character mapping
steps.body: Each InfiniBot agent can speak as its own Robovoice character. Agents without a mapping use the default.

steps.title: Pipelines
steps.body: The effective STT → LLM → TTS chain for each mapped character. Pipelines are edited in the Robovoice dashboard; this card is read-only.

steps.title: InfiniBot tools for Robovoice
steps.body: Robovoice characters can call a curated set of InfiniBot tools through this MCP endpoint.

walkthroughs.title: Choose the voice provider
walkthroughs.summary: Auto, built-in or Robovoice, and how fallback works.

steps.title: Provider status
steps.body: The dot and title say what serves voice right now. Green means ready; amber means there is a warning, such as a missing URL.

steps.title: Auto, built-in or Robovoice
steps.body: **Auto** (the default) uses local voice. Cloud voice (Robovoice) is only used when you pick it by name. Switching takes effect without a restart.

practice.note: Not changed in this tour: picking a provider switches voice for everyone on this gateway.

steps.title: Voice never breaks
steps.body: Under Auto, voice stays local even with the Robovoice plugin on. Pick Cloud voice (Robovoice) yourself to use it; anything it can't serve falls back to local voice.

walkthroughs.title: Link your Robovoice
walkthroughs.summary: Self-hosted or cloud, URL, device id and the write-only secrets.

steps.title: Where Robovoice runs
steps.body: Choose **Self-hosted** for your own Robovoice stack or **Robovoice cloud** for robovoice.io. Click **Robovoice cloud** to see its extra field. This only changes the form.

steps.title: The Robovoice URL
steps.body: For cloud this is `https://robovoice.io`; self-hosted is usually `http://<host>:3011`. Type it to try the field. It isn't saved until you press **Save**.

steps.title: Edge device id
steps.body: The name this gateway uses as a Robovoice edge device, for example `infinibot-gateway`.

steps.title: Edge token from robovoice login
steps.body: On cloud, run `robovoice login` in the Robovoice CLI and paste the `rve_…` edge token here. Self-hosted stacks with a strict device policy use the **Device key** field instead.

practice.note: Never paste a real token during a tour. Secrets are write-only: once saved the page only shows a masked hint, and Remove saved clears them.

steps.title: Location and expressive tier
steps.body: An optional Robovoice location id applies that location's pipeline overrides.

steps.title: Test, then save
steps.body: **Test connection** checks Robovoice's health and character list only. **Save** stores the settings and secrets, then reloads characters and pipelines.

practice.note: Not pressed here. Saving and testing are admin-only (robovoice.settings.set, robovoice.test). Leave the page to discard the draft you typed.

walkthroughs.title: Map agents to characters
walkthroughs.summary: Default character, per-agent mapping and the pipeline safety labels.

steps.title: The default character
steps.body: Agents without their own mapping speak as this character. **Robovoice decides** uses Robovoice's active character. The list fills in once Robovoice is connected.

steps.title: One row per agent
steps.body: Pick a character for any agent, such as `main` or an AI employee. A change is saved as soon as you pick. The Voice column shows the character's TTS provider and language.

steps.title: Read a pipeline
steps.body: Each mapped character lists its **STT**, **LLM** and **TTS** stage with provider, model and state. With nothing connected yet, the card says so.

steps.title: Self-host only labels
steps.body: Some models, such as openWakeWord's bundled wake words and Piper Lessac voices, are non-commercial. They're labelled **Self-host only**, and on a cloud deployment the warning turns red so you swap them before offering calls to others.

walkthroughs.title: Fair use and agent tools
walkthroughs.summary: How free cloud voice stays fair, and the MCP endpoint for Robovoice characters.

steps.title: Free, with fair use
steps.body: Cloud voice costs nothing. This card shows this month's minutes so usage stays fair. If cloud voice is busy or you hit the daily fair-use limit, switch to local voice in one click.

steps.title: The MCP endpoint
steps.body: Point a Robovoice MCP server at this address with transport `streamable_http` and your gateway token. Characters can then use the listed InfiniBot tools during a call.

steps.title: A curated tool set
steps.body: By default Robovoice gets a curated set (notes, kanban, research, workflows, sessions_spawn, claude_coder and more), not every tool. Give tool access only to characters you trust.

quiz.prompt: Voice is on **Auto** and you turn on the Robovoice plugin but haven't saved a URL. What serves voice?
options: Local voice: Auto never switches to Robovoice on its own
quiz.explain: Local voice is the default. Cloud voice (Robovoice) is only used when you pick it yourself, and it's free.

quiz.prompt: Where does the `rve_…` edge token for Robovoice cloud come from?
options: It is generated by this page
quiz.explain: `robovoice login` issues the org-scoped edge token you paste into the Edge token field.

options: It places a short test call
Robovoice's health and character list only
Every agent's pipeline end to end
quiz.explain: The test only reads Robovoice's health and character list. It never places a call.

quiz.prompt: Why is a model labelled **Self-host only**?
options: It is too slow for the cloud
Its licence is non-commercial, so don't charge for calls that use it
quiz.explain: openWakeWord's bundled weights and Piper Lessac voices are non-commercial; on cloud the label becomes an error to swap them.
